en: Peirce on Abduction
zh: 皮尔士论溯因

en: The term “abduction” was coined by Charles Sanders Peirce in his work on the logic of science. He introduced it to denote a type of non-deductive inference that was different from the already familiar inductive type. It is a common complaint that no coherent picture emerges from Peirce’s writings on abduction. (Though perhaps this is not surprising, given that he worked on abduction throughout his career, which spanned a period of more than fifty years. For a concise yet thorough account of the development of Peirce’s thoughts about abduction, see Fann 1970.) Yet it is clear that, as Peirce understood the term, “abduction” did not quite mean what it is currently taken to mean (see Campos 2011 and McAuliffe 2015). One main difference between his conception and the modern one is that, whereas according to the latter, abduction belongs to what the logical empiricists called the “context of justification”—the stage of scientific inquiry in which we are concerned with the assessment of theories—for Peirce abduction had its proper place in the context of discovery, the stage of inquiry in which we try to generate theories which may then later be assessed. As he says, “[a]bduction is the process of forming explanatory hypotheses. It is the only logical operation which introduces any new idea” (CP 5.172); elsewhere he says that abduction encompasses “all the operations by which theories and conceptions are engendered” (CP 5.590). Deduction and induction, then, come into play at the later stage of theory assessment: deduction helps to derive testable consequences from the explanatory hypotheses that abduction has helped us to conceive, and induction finally helps us to reach a verdict on the hypotheses, where the nature of the verdict is dependent on the number of testable consequences that have been verified. (As an aside, it is to be noted that Gerhard Schurz has recently defended a view of abduction that is again very much in the Peircean spirit. On this view, “the crucial function of a pattern of abduction … consists in its function as a search strategy which leads us, for a given kind of scenario, in a reasonable time to a most promising explanatory conjecture which is then subject to further test” (Schurz 2008, 205). The paper is also of interest because of the useful typology of patterns of abduction that it puts forth.)
zh: “溯因”（abduction）一词是查尔斯·桑德斯·皮尔士（Charles Sanders Peirce）在其关于科学逻辑的工作中铸造的。他引入这个词，是为了指称一种不同于人们已熟悉的归纳类型的非演绎推理。人们常有这样的抱怨：从皮尔士关于溯因的著述中拼不出一幅融贯的图景。（不过这也许并不奇怪，因为他毕生都在研究溯因，其跨度超过五十年。关于皮尔士溯因思想发展的简明而周全的叙述，见 Fann 1970。）然而清楚的是，按皮尔士对该词的理解，“溯因”并不完全等于它如今被赋予的含义（见 Campos 2011 与 McAuliffe 2015）。他的构想（conception）与现代构想之间的一个主要差别是：按现代构想，溯因属于逻辑经验主义者所谓的“辩护语境”（context of justification）——即科学探究中我们关心理论评估的那个阶段——而对皮尔士来说，溯因的适当位置在发现的语境（context of discovery），即探究中我们力图生成理论、而这些理论随后再受评估的阶段。如他所说，“溯因是形成解释性假说的过程。它是引入任何新观念的唯一逻辑操作”（CP 5.172）；在别处他又说，溯因涵盖了“所有借以产生理论与概念的操作”（CP 5.590）。于是，演绎与归纳在稍后的理论评估阶段登场：演绎帮助从溯因帮助我们想出的解释性假说中导出可检验的推论，归纳最终帮助我们对这些假说作出裁决，而裁决的性质取决于得到验证的可检验推论的数量。（附带应当注意到，格哈德·舒尔茨（Gerhard Schurz）近来辩护了一种再度非常合乎皮尔士精神的溯因观。按这种观点，“一个溯因模式的关键功能……在于它作为一种搜索策略，使我们对于给定类型的事态，能在合理的时间内得到一个最有希望的解释性猜想，然后该猜想再接受进一步的检验”（Schurz 2008, 205）。这篇文章之所以也值得一读，还因为它提出了一个有用的溯因模式类型学。）

en: As Harry Frankfurt (1958) has noted, however, the foregoing view is not as easy to make sense of as might at first appear. Abduction is supposed to be part of the logic of science, but what exactly is *logical *about inventing explanatory hypotheses? According to Peirce (CP 5.189), abduction belongs to logic because it can be given a schematic characterization, to wit, the following:
zh: 然而，正如哈里·法兰克福（Harry Frankfurt，1958）所指出的，上述观点并不像乍看之下那样容易讲得通。溯因本应是科学逻辑的一部分，但发明解释性假说这件事究竟有什么是*逻辑的*？按皮尔士（CP 5.189）的说法，溯因属于逻辑，因为它可以得到一个图式化的刻画，即：

en: The surprising fact, *C*, is observed. But if *A* were true, *C* would be a matter of course. Hence, there is reason to suspect that *A* is true.
zh: 令人惊讶的事实 *C* 被观察到了。但如果 *A* 为真，则 *C* 就是理所当然的了。因此，有理由怀疑 *A* 为真。

en: But Frankfurt rightly remarks that this is not an inference leading to any new idea. After all, the new idea—the explanatory hypothesis *A*—must have occurred to one *before *one infers that there is reason to suspect that *A* is true, for *A* already figures in the second premise.
zh: 但法兰克福正确地评论道：这并不是一个导向任何新观念的推理。毕竟，新观念——解释性假说 *A*——必定在一个人推断“有理由怀疑 *A* 为真”*之前*就已经出现了，因为 *A* 已经出现在第二个前提之中。

en: Frankfurt then goes on to argue that a number of passages in Peirce’s work suggest an understanding of abduction not so much as a process of *inventing *hypotheses but rather as one of *adopting *hypotheses, where the adoption of the hypothesis is not as being true or verified or confirmed, but as being a worthy candidate for further investigation. On this understanding, abduction could still be thought of as being part of the context of discovery. It would work as a kind of selection function, or filter, determining which of the hypotheses that have been conceived in the stage of discovery are to pass to the next stage and be subjected to empirical testing. The selection criterion is that there must be a reason to suspect that the hypothesis is true, and we will have such a reason if the hypothesis makes whichever observed facts we are interested in explaining a matter of course. This would indeed make better sense of Peirce’s claim that abduction is a logical operation.
zh: 法兰克福接着论证，皮尔士著述中的许多段落提示了一种理解：溯因与其说是*发明*假说的过程，不如说是*采纳*假说的过程——这里的采纳不是作为真、得到验证或得到确证，而是作为值得进一步考察的候选者。按这种理解，溯因仍可被视为发现语境的一部分。它将作为一种选择函数或过滤器发挥作用，决定在发现阶段被想出的诸假说中哪些可以进入下一阶段、接受经验检验。选择标准是：必须有理由怀疑该假说为真；而如果该假说使我们感兴趣想要解释的那些被观察到的事实成为理所当然，我们就会有这样的理由。这确实能更好地讲通皮尔士关于溯因是一种逻辑操作的主张。

en: Nevertheless, Frankfurt ultimately rejects this proposal as well. Given, he says, that there may be infinitely many hypotheses that account for a given fact or set of facts—which Peirce acknowledged—it can hardly be a sufficient condition for the adoption of a hypothesis (in the above sense) that its truth would make that fact or set of facts a matter of course. At a minimum, abduction would not seem to be of much use as a selection function. One may doubt whether this is a valid objection, however. Echoing what was said in connection with underdetermination arguments, we note that it is by no means clear that “accounting for a given fact” is to be identified with “making that fact a matter of course.” For all Frankfurt says, for a hypothesis to account for a fact, it is enough if it entails that fact. But virtually no philosopher of science nowadays holds that entailment is sufficient for explanation. And it would seem reasonable to read the phrase “making a given fact a matter of course” as “giving a satisfactory explanation of that fact.” In response to Frankfurt’s objection, it could thus be argued that even if there is an infinity of hypotheses that account for a given fact, there may still be only a handful that could be said to give a satisfactory explanation of it. But it is for Peirce scholars to decide whether this proposed interpretation is plausible in the light of Peirce’s further writings.
zh: 尽管如此，法兰克福最终也拒绝了这一方案。他说，考虑到可以对一个给定事实或一组事实作出说明的假说也许有无穷多个——皮尔士本人承认这一点——“其真会使该事实或该组事实成为理所当然”很难成为采纳一个假说（在上述意义上）的充分条件。至少，作为选择函数，溯因看来派不上多大用场。然而人们可以怀疑这是不是一个有效的反驳。呼应关于不充分决定性论证的讨论，我们指出：“说明一个给定事实”是否可以等同于“使该事实成为理所当然”，绝不明确。就法兰克福所说而言，一个假说只要蕴含那个事实，就算说明了它。但如今几乎没有科学哲学家还认为蕴含对于解释来说是充分的。而把“使一个给定事实成为理所当然”读作“对该事实给出一个令人满意的解释”，似乎也是合理的。作为对法兰克福反驳的回应，因此可以论证说：即便说明一个给定事实的假说有无穷多个，可以说对该事实给出令人满意解释的假说也许仍只有寥寥几个。至于这一拟议的解读在皮尔士进一步著作的观照下是否可信，则应由皮尔士学者来裁定。

en: Even if “making a given fact a matter of course” can be read as “giving a satisfactory explanation of that fact,” it is remarkable that there is no reference in Peirce’s writings on abduction to the notion of *best *explanation. Some satisfactory explanations might still be better than others, and there might even be a unique best one. This idea is crucial in all recent thinking about abduction. Therein lies another main difference between Peirce’s conception of abduction and the modern one.
zh: 即便“使一个给定事实成为理所当然”可以读作“对该事实给出一个令人满意的解释”，值得注意的是，皮尔士关于溯因的著述中完全没有提到*最佳*解释的概念。某些令人满意的解释可能仍比另一些更好，甚至可能存在唯一最佳的一个。这一观念在近来所有关于溯因的思考中都至关重要。这正是皮尔士的溯因构想与现代构想之间的另一个主要差别。

en: Alcmaeon
zh: 克罗顿的阿尔克迈翁 Alcmaeon (Carl Huffman)

en: **First published Thu Apr 10, 2003; substantive revision Fri Jul 18, 2025**
zh: *首次发表于 2003 年 4 月 10 日；2025 年 7 月 18 日实质修订。*

en: Alcmaeon of Croton was an early Greek medical writer and philosopher-scientist. His exact date, his relationship to other early Greek philosopher-scientists, and whether he was primarily a medical writer/physician or a Presocratic cosmologist, are all matters of controversy. He is likely to have written his book sometime between 500 and 450 BCE. The surviving fragments and testimonia focus primarily on issues of physiology, psychology, and epistemology and reveal Alcmaeon to be a thinker of considerable originality. He was the first to identify the brain as the seat of understanding and to distinguish understanding from perception. Alcmaeon thought that the sensory organs were connected to the brain by channels (*poroi*) and may have discovered the *poroi* connecting the eyes to the brain (i.e. the optic nerve) by excising the eyeball of an animal, although it is doubtful that he used dissection as a standard method. He developed the first argument on record in the Greek tradition for the immortality of the soul. He used a political metaphor to define health and disease: The equality (*isonomia*) of the opposing powers which make up the body (e.g., the wet, the dry, the hot, the cold, the sweet, the bitter etc.) preserves health, whereas the monarchy of any one of them produces disease. Alcmaeon discussed a wide range of topics in physiology including sleep, death, and the development of the embryo. It is unclear whether he also presented a cosmology in terms of opposing powers, but we do have some testimonia concerning his views on astronomy. Alcmaeon had considerable impact on his successors in the Greek philosophical tradition. Aristotle wrote a treatise responding to him, Plato may have been influenced by his argument for the immortality of the soul, and both Plato and Philolaus accepted his view that the brain is the seat of intelligence.
zh: 克罗顿的阿尔克迈翁（Alcmaeon of Croton）是一位早期希腊医学作家兼哲学家-科学家。他的确切年代、他与其他早期希腊哲学家-科学家的关系，以及他究竟主要是医学作家/医生还是前苏格拉底宇宙论者，全都是争论未决的问题。他的著作很可能写于公元前 500 至 450 年之间。流传下来的残篇与学说汇编条目主要集中于生理学、心理学和认识论问题，显示出阿尔克迈翁是一位原创性相当高的思想家。他是第一个把大脑确认为理解之所在、并把理解与知觉区分开来的人。阿尔克迈翁认为感觉器官通过通道（poroi）与大脑相连，而且他可能是通过切除动物的眼球发现了连接眼睛与大脑的通道（即视神经），尽管他是否把解剖当作常规方法颇可怀疑。他提出了希腊传统中有案可查的第一个灵魂不朽论证。他用一个政治隐喻来定义健康与疾病：构成身体的诸对立力量（如湿与干、热与冷、甜与苦等等）的平等（isonomia）维系着健康，而其中任何一种力量的专权（monarchia）则导致疾病。阿尔克迈翁讨论的生理学话题很广，包括睡眠、死亡和胚胎的发育。他是否也用对立力量提出过一套宇宙论，尚不清楚，但我们确实有一些关于他天文学观点的学说汇编条目。阿尔克迈翁对希腊哲学传统中的后继者影响可观：亚里士多德写过一部专著回应他，柏拉图可能受他灵魂不朽论证的影响，柏拉图和菲洛劳斯都接受了他关于大脑是智慧之所在的观点。

en: Life and Works
zh: 1 生平与著作

en: 1.1 Physician Philosopher?
zh: 1.1 医生还是哲学家？

en: Alcmaeon, son of Peirithous (otherwise unknown), lived in the Greek city of Croton on the instep of the boot of Italy. Diogenes Laertius, in his brief life of Alcmaeon (VIII. 83), asserts that he wrote mostly on medical matters. There is, however, little direct evidence for his work as a practicing physician. Later writers in the medical tradition, such as Galen (DK A2), treat him as a philosopher-scientist rather than as a physician, so that some scholars (Mansfeld 1975; cf. Perilli 2001 for a critique)[^mansfeld-1975][^perilli-2001] have concluded that he was not a doctor at all but rather a Presocratic *physiologos* (writer on nature). In unpublished notes, however, Gregory Vlastos argues that Aristotle’s failure to include Alcmaeon in his survey of the views of the Presocratic *physiologoi* in his *Metaphysics* and *Physics* clearly shows that he knew of no cosmology put forth by Alcmaeon (Vassallo 2021: 173)[^vassallo-2021]. Indeed, the majority of scholars, because of Diogenes’ remark and because of the focus on the functioning of the human body in the testimonia and fragments, refer to Alcmaeon as a physician-philosopher. The historian Herodotus tells us that, in the second half of the sixth century, the physicians of Croton were the best in the Greek world (III. 131) and recounts in some detail the activities of the most prominent Crotoniate physician of the time, Democedes (III. 125–138). Thus, whether a practicing physician or not, Alcmaeon undoubtedly owes some of his interest in human physiology and psychology to the medical tradition in Croton. In the fifth century, it is difficult to draw clear lines between the work of a medical writer/physician and a philosopher/scientist. Presocratic cosmologies of this period devoted some attention to questions of human physiology and medicine, and conversely the early treatises in the Hippocratic corpus often paid some attention to cosmology (see Aristotle, *Resp*. 480b23 ff.). The earliest Presocratic cosmologies in Ionia (e.g., those of Anaximander and Anaximenes) did not deal with physiology, and it is possible that the new interest in physiology in cosmologies of the fifth century (e.g., those of Empedocles and Anaxagoras) was due to the influence of Alcmaeon (Zhmud 2012a, 366; 2014, 100)[^zhmud-2012a]. Année argues that asking whether he was a “medical writer or philosopher” is the wrong question and instead asks whether Alcmaeon wrote a “scientific treatise in prose or a medical poem” (2019: 15).
zh: 阿尔克迈翁是佩里托奥斯（Peirithous，此人生平不详）之子，住在意大利长靴脚背处的希腊城市克罗顿。第欧根尼·拉尔修在他为阿尔克迈翁所写的短传（VIII. 83）中断言，阿尔克迈翁的写作大多涉及医学。然而，关于他行医实践的直接证据很少。医学传统中的晚期作家，如盖伦（DK A2），把他当作哲学家-科学家而非医生来对待，因此一些学者（Mansfeld 1975；另见 Perilli 2001 的批评）得出结论：他根本不是医生，而是一位前苏格拉底的论自然者（physiologos，即论述自然的作家）。不过，Gregory Vlastos 在未刊笔记中指出，亚里士多德在《形而上学》和《物理学》里综述前苏格拉底论自然者的观点时没有把阿尔克迈翁包括在内，这清楚地表明他不知道阿尔克迈翁提出过任何宇宙论（Vassallo 2021: 173）。事实上，多数学者——由于第欧根尼的评述，也由于学说汇编条目和残篇聚焦于人体机能——都称阿尔克迈翁为医生-哲学家。历史学家希罗多德告诉我们，公元前六世纪下半叶，克罗顿的医生是希腊世界最好的（III. 131），他还相当详细地记述了当时最杰出的克罗顿医生德摩塞迪斯的活动（III. 125–138）。因此，无论阿尔克迈翁是否行医，他对人体生理学和心理学的部分兴趣无疑来自克罗顿的医学传统。在公元前五世纪，医学作家/医生的工作与哲学家/科学家的工作之间很难划出清晰的界线。这一时期的前苏格拉底宇宙论对人的生理学和医学问题有所关注；反过来，希波克拉底文集中的早期论著也常常留意宇宙论（参见亚里士多德，Resp. 480b23 以下）。爱奥尼亚最早的前苏格拉底宇宙论（如阿那克西曼德和阿那克西美尼的宇宙论）并不涉及生理学，而公元前五世纪宇宙论（如恩培多克勒和阿那克萨戈拉的宇宙论）中对生理学的新兴趣，有可能正是受了阿尔克迈翁的影响（Zhmud 2012a, 366; 2014, 100）。Année 主张，“医学作家还是哲学家”这个问法本身就问错了，真正该问的是阿尔克迈翁写的是“散文体的科学论著还是一首医学诗”（2019: 15）。

en: 1.2 Was Alcmaeon a Pythagorean?
zh: 1.2 阿尔克迈翁是毕达哥拉斯学派成员吗？

en: Croton is also famous as the center of Pythagoras’ activity from ca. 530, when he left Samos. Alcmaeon addressed his book to three men who may have been Pythagoreans:
zh: 克罗顿还有一层名声：大约自公元前 530 年离开萨摩斯岛起，毕达哥拉斯就以克罗顿为活动中心。阿尔克迈翁把他的著作题献给三个人，这三个人可能是毕达哥拉斯学派成员：

en: Alcmaeon of Croton, son of Peirithous, said the following to Brotinus, Leon, and Bathyllus… (DK 12B1)
zh: 克罗顿的阿尔克迈翁，佩里托奥斯之子，对布罗提努斯（Brotinus）、里昂（Leon）和巴提卢斯（Bathyllus）说了如下的话……（DK 12B1）

en: We know nothing of Leon and Bathyllus, except that Iamblichus, in *On the Pythagorean Way of Life* (=*VP*), lists a Pythagorean named Leon from Metapontum and a Pythagorean Bathylaus from Poseidonia (Paestum), both Greek cities of southern Italy (*VP* 267). Bro(n)tinus is identified as a Pythagorean from Croton in some places (D.L. VIII. 42; Iamb. *VP* 132) and from Metapontum in others (*VP* 194, 267). He is either the father or the husband of Theano, who is in turn either the wife or student of Pythagoras. Does this “dedication” of his book to Pythagoreans indicate that Alcmaeon himself was a Pythagorean? Even if this is a dedication, it does not follow that Alcmaeon agreed with the views of his addressees. Comparison with Empedocles’ address to Pausanias suggests, moreover, that what we have is not a dedication but an exhortation or an attempt to instruct (Vlastos 1953, 344, n. 25)[^vlastos-1953]. Comparison with other early Greek prose writers such as Hecataeus and Heraclitus shows that books could begin with criticism of the views of others so that Alcmaeon’s address to these Pythagoreans may be polemical (Kouloumentas 2018).
zh: 关于里昂和巴提卢斯，我们一无所知，只知道扬布里柯在《论毕达哥拉斯式生活》（=VP）中列有一位来自梅塔蓬图姆的毕达哥拉斯学派成员里昂，和一位来自波塞多尼亚（帕埃斯图姆）的毕达哥拉斯学派成员巴提卢斯，两座城市都是南意大利的希腊城市（VP 267）。布罗提努斯在有些文献中被认定为来自克罗顿的毕达哥拉斯学派成员（D.L. VIII. 42；Iamb. VP 132），在另一些文献中则来自梅塔蓬图姆（VP 194, 267）。他要么是 Theano 的父亲，要么是她的丈夫，而 Theano 又要么是毕达哥拉斯的妻子，要么是他的学生。把著作“题献”给毕达哥拉斯学派成员，是否表明阿尔克迈翁本人也是其中一员？即便这真是一条题献，也推不出阿尔克迈翁赞同受献者的观点。而且，与恩培多克勒对 Pausanias 的献辞相比较，可以提示我们：我们看到的不是题献，而是劝诫或试图施教（Vlastos 1953, 344, n. 25）。与其他早期希腊散文作家（如 Hecataeus 和赫拉克利特）的著作相比还可以看出，当时的书完全可以以批评他人观点开篇，因此阿尔克迈翁对这几位毕达哥拉斯学派成员的致辞也可能是论战性的（Kouloumentas 2018）。

en: Diogenes Laertius, in his *Lives of the Philosophers* (3ʳᵈ century AD), includes Alcmaeon among the Pythagoreans and says that he studied with Pythagoras (VIII. 83). Later authors such as Iamblichus (*VP* 104, 267), Philoponus (*De An.* p. 88), and the scholiast on Plato (*Alc*. 121e) also call Alcmaeon a Pythagorean. A majority of scholars up to the middle of the twentieth century followed this tradition. However, it is not true that the ancient “tradition is unanimous in presenting him as a Pythagorean” (Zhmud 2012a, 123)[^zhmud-2012a]. In fact, the majority of ancient sources do not describe him as a Pythagorean (e.g., Clement [DK 24A2], Galen [DK24A2], Aetius [DK 24A4, 6, 8–10, 13, 17–18], Censorinus [DK 24A13–14], and Chalcidius [DK A10]). The best argument for regarding him as Pythagorean would be his inclusion in Iamblichus’ catalogue of Pythagoreans at the end of his *On the Pythagorean Life*, if we could be sure that all parts of that catalogue go back to Aristoxenus in the fourth century, since Aristoxenus is a very knowledgeable source on Pythagoreanism (Zhmud 2012a, 122; 2012b, 241–43)[^zhmud-2012a]. However, certain parts of the catalogue are very unlikely to go back to Aristoxenus and we cannot be certain that the inclusion of Alcmaeon was due to him (Huffman 2005, 297–99). Apart from this possibility regarding Aristoxenus, no one earlier than Diogenes Laertius (ca. 200 AD) calls Alcmaeon a Pythagorean. Aristotle wrote two books on the Pythagoreans but wrote a separate book on Alcmaeon. Aristotle and Theophrastus refer to him a number of times but never identify him as a Pythagorean, and this is the practice of the doxographical tradition (see A4, 6, 8–10, 13–14, 17–18, in *DK* 24). Simplicius (6ᵗʰ AD) reports that some have handed down the view that Alcmaeon is a Pythagorean but notes that Aristotle denies it (*De An.* 32.3). Most telling is Aristotle’s discussion of Alcmaeon in *Metaphysics* book I (986a22 ff.). He notes a similarity between Alcmaeon and a group of Pythagoreans in positing opposites as the principles of things but expresses uncertainty as to who influenced whom. Earlier scholars took this comparison of Alcmaeon to the Pythagoreans as confirmation that he was a Pythagorean. Most scholars of the last fifty years, however, have come to recognize that Aristotle’s treatment of Alcmaeon here suggests the exact opposite; it only makes sense to compare him with the Pythagoreans and wonder who influenced whom, if he is not a Pythagorean (e.g., Guthrie 1962, 341: “Aristotle … expressly distinguishes him from the Pythagoreans”)[^guthrie-1962]. Certainly most of the opposites which are mentioned as crucial to Alcmaeon do not appear in the Pythagorean table of opposites, and there is no trace of the crucial Pythagorean opposition between limit and unlimited in Alcmaeon. The overwhelming majority of scholars since 1950 have accordingly regarded Alcmaeon as a figure independent of the Pythagoreans (e.g., Guthrie 1962, 341; Burkert 1972, 289; KRS 1983, 339; Lloyd 1991, 167; Kahn 2001; Riedweg 2005, 115; Primavesi 2012, 447; Année 2019: 99–100. Zhmud [2012a, 121–124; 2014, 97–102] is the notable exception)[^année-2019][^guthrie-1962][^kahn-2001][^kirk-1983][^lloyd-1991][^primavesi-2012][^riedweg-2005], although, as a fellow citizen of Croton, he will have been familiar with their thought.
zh: 第欧根尼·拉尔修在《名哲言行录》（公元 3 世纪）中把阿尔克迈翁列入毕达哥拉斯学派，并说他曾随毕达哥拉斯学习（VIII. 83）。晚期作家如扬布里柯（VP 104, 267）、Philoponus（De An. p. 88）以及柏拉图注疏家（Alc. 121e）也称阿尔克迈翁为毕达哥拉斯学派成员。二十世纪中叶以前的多数学者沿袭了这一传统。然而，“古代传统众口一词地把他说成毕达哥拉斯学派成员”并不属实（Zhmud 2012a, 123）。事实上，多数古代文献并没有这样描述他（如 Clement [DK 24A2]、盖伦 [DK24A2]、Aetius [DK 24A4, 6, 8–10, 13, 17–18]、Censorinus [DK 24A13–14] 和 Chalcidius [DK A10]）。把他视为毕达哥拉斯学派成员的最佳论据，是扬布里柯在《论毕达哥拉斯式生活》卷末的毕达哥拉斯学派名录中收了他——前提是我们能确定该名录的各部分都源自公元前四世纪的 Aristoxenus，因为 Aristoxenus 是毕达哥拉斯主义的可靠知情人（Zhmud 2012a, 122; 2012b, 241–43）。然而，名录的某些部分几乎不可能出自 Aristoxenus，我们也无法确定收编阿尔克迈翁是出于他之手（Huffman 2005, 297–99）。撇开这一与 Aristoxenus 有关的可能不谈，在第欧根尼·拉尔修（约公元 200 年）之前没有人称阿尔克迈翁为毕达哥拉斯学派成员。亚里士多德写过两部关于毕达哥拉斯学派的书，却另写了一部专论阿尔克迈翁的书。亚里士多德和特奥弗拉斯托斯多次提到他，却从不把他称作毕达哥拉斯学派成员，学说汇编传统也是如此做法（见 DK 24 中的 A4, 6, 8–10, 13–14, 17–18）。辛普里丘（公元 6 世纪）报告说，有人传下阿尔克迈翁是毕达哥拉斯学派成员的说法，但指出亚里士多德否认这一点（De An. 32.3）。最有说服力的是亚里士多德在《形而上学》第一卷（986a22 以下）对阿尔克迈翁的讨论：他指出阿尔克迈翁与一群毕达哥拉斯学派成员在把对立当作万物的本原这点上相似，但表示不确定是谁影响了谁。早先的学者把亚里士多德对阿尔克迈翁与毕达哥拉斯学派的这一比较当作他是学派成员的佐证。而近五十年的多数学者逐渐认识到，亚里士多德在这里的处理恰恰指向相反的结论：只有当阿尔克迈翁不是毕达哥拉斯学派成员时，把他与该学派比较并追问谁影响了谁才有意义（如 Guthrie 1962, 341：“亚里士多德……明确把他与毕达哥拉斯学派区别开来”）。诚然，被说成对阿尔克迈翁至关重要的那些对立，大多并不见于毕达哥拉斯学派的对立表；而毕达哥拉斯学派关键的“限与无定”对立，在阿尔克迈翁那里也毫无踪迹。因此，1950 年以来绝大多数论者把阿尔克迈翁视为独立于毕达哥拉斯学派的人物（如 Guthrie 1962, 341；Burkert 1972, 289；KRS 1983, 339；Lloyd 1991, 167；Kahn 2001；Riedweg 2005, 115；Primavesi 2012, 447；Année 2019: 99–100。Zhmud [2012a, 121–124; 2014, 97–102] 是显著的例外），不过，作为克罗顿的同城人，他必定熟悉该学派的思想。

en: 1.3 Date
zh: 1.3 年代

en: No issue concerning Alcmaeon has been more controversial than his date. Some have sought to date him on the basis of his address to Brotinus (e.g., Zhmud 2012a, 122)[^zhmud-2012a]. Brotinus’ dates are too uncertain to be of much help, however. If he is Theano’s father and Theano was Pythagoras’ wife, he could be a contemporary of Pythagoras (570–490) or even older. If he is Theano’s husband and she was a student of Pythagoras in his old age and thus twenty in 490, Brotinus could have been born as late as 520. This suggests that Brotinus could have been the addressee of the book any time between 550 and 450 BCE. The center of controversy, however, has been a sentence in the passage of Aristotle’s *Metaphysics* discussed above:
zh: 关于阿尔克迈翁，没有哪个问题比他的年代更有争议。有人试图根据他对布罗提努斯的致辞来定年（如 Zhmud 2012a, 122）。然而布罗提努斯的年代太不确定，帮不上什么忙。如果他是 Theano 的父亲，而 Theano 是毕达哥拉斯的妻子，他可能与毕达哥拉斯（前 570–490）同时代甚至更年长。如果他是 Theano 的丈夫，而她在毕达哥拉斯晚年拜师、因而在前 490 年时二十岁，那么布罗提努斯的出生最晚可到前 520 年。这意味着布罗提努斯可能在前 550 至 450 年之间的任何时刻受献此书。然而，争论的焦点是上面讨论过的《形而上学》那一段里的一句话：

en: Alcmaeon of Croton also seems to have thought along similar lines, and either he took this theory over from them [i.e. the Pythagoreans] or they from him. **For in age Alcmaeon was in the old age of Pythagoras**, and his views were similar to theirs (986a27–31).
zh: 克罗顿的阿尔克迈翁似乎也持类似的理论，或者是他从他们[即毕达哥拉斯学派]那里取来了这个理论，或者是他们从他那里取来的。因为阿尔克迈翁年届毕达哥拉斯之暮年，而他们的学说彼此相似（986a27–31）。

en: The sentence in bold above is missing in one of the major manuscripts and Alexander makes no mention of it in his commentary on the *Metaphysics*. It does appear in the other two major manuscripts and in Asclepius’ commentary. A number of scholars have regarded it as a remark by a later commentator, which has crept into the text (e.g., Ross 1924, 152; Burkert 1972, 29, n.60) and this is the view of the most recent editor (Primavesi 2012, 447–8)[^primavesi-2012]. It is a surprising remark for Aristotle to make, since he only refers to Pythagoras once elsewhere in all his extant writings and throughout this passage of the *Metaphysics* refers to the Pythagoreans or Italians in the plural. Other scholars regard the remark as genuine (e.g., Wachtler 1896; Guthrie 1962, 341–3; Zhmud 2012a, 122)[^wachtler-1896][^guthrie-1962][^zhmud-2012a]. Even if we accept the remark as genuine, the assertion that Alcmaeon “was” (*egeneto*) in the old age of Pythagoras is ambiguous. Does it mean that Alcmaeon was born in the old age of Pythagoras, or that he lived (flourished?) in the old age of Pythagoras? Diels emended the sentence to say that Alcmaeon was “young” in the old age of Pythagoras and this emendation is supported by a similar remark found in Iamblichus (*VP* 104). Although Diels accepted the text as Aristotelian, others have seen the parallel with Iamblichus as evidence that it is a remark by a later commentator and have pointed out that the report in Iamblichus involves several chronological impossibilities (e.g., that Philolaus was young in the old age of Pythagoras). Moreover, Diels’ text suggests that the purpose of the remark was to show Alcmaeon’s dependence on Pythagoras, which would show that the remark cannot be due to Aristotle, who has just distinguished Alcmaeon from the Pythagoreans and expressed doubts as to who influenced whom (Primavesi 2012, 447–8)[^primavesi-2012]. Even if the remark is unlikely to go back to Aristotle, his doubts about who influenced whom suggest that Alcmaeon belonged to the late sixth or early fifth century (Schofield 2012, 156)[^schofield-2012], which would argue against the late date of 440 adopted by Mansfeld (2013, 78, n. 1). One group of scholars thus dates the publication of Alcmaeon’s book to around 500 (Burkert 1972, 292; Kirk, Raven, Schofield 1983, 339 [early 5ᵗʰ]; Zhmud 2012a, 122 [not later than 490])[^zhmud-2012a] so that he would have been born around 540. Another group has him born around 510 so that his book would have been published in 470 or later (Guthrie 1962, 358 [480–440 BCE]; Lloyd 1991, 168 [490–430 BCE])[^guthrie-1962][^lloyd-1991]. In either case Alcmaeon probably wrote before Empedocles, Anaxagoras, and Philolaus. He is either the contemporary or the predecessor of Parmenides. Attempts to date him on the basis of internal evidence alone, i.e. comparison of his doctrines with those of other thinkers, have led to the widest divergence of dates. Edelstein says that he may have lived in the late fifth century (1942, 372), while Lebedev makes him active in the late 6ᵗʰ (1993). Année has proposed the earliest dating for Alcmaeon, suggesting that he was active in the middle of the sixth century and the contemporary of Pythagoras (2019: 101).
zh: 加粗的那句话在一部重要抄本中缺失，Alexander 在他给《形而上学》作的注疏中也没有提到它。它确实出现在另外两部重要抄本和 Asclepius 的注疏中。不少学者认为它是后世注疏家的评语，窜入了正文（如 Ross 1924, 152；Burkert 1972, 29, n.60），最新校勘本的编者（Primavesi 2012, 447–8）也持此见。亚里士多德说这话令人惊讶，因为在他全部传世著作中，他只在别处提到过毕达哥拉斯一次，而且在这整段《形而上学》文字里都用复数称呼毕达哥拉斯学派成员或意大利人。另一些学者则认为这句话是真作（如 Wachtler 1896；Guthrie 1962, 341–3；Zhmud 2012a, 122）。即便承认这句话出自亚里士多德，“阿尔克迈翁生（egeneto）于毕达哥拉斯暮年”这句话也是有歧义的：它是指阿尔克迈翁出生于毕达哥拉斯的暮年，还是指他生活（盛年？）于毕达哥拉斯的暮年？Diels 把这句话校改为“阿尔克迈翁年幼于毕达哥拉斯之暮年”，扬布里柯书中一句类似的话（VP 104）支持这一校改。虽然 Diels 接受了这句话为亚里士多德手笔，另一些学者却把与扬布里柯的平行文本看作后世注疏家手笔的证据，并指出扬布里柯的报告包含好几处年代上的不可能（例如菲洛劳斯“年幼于毕达哥拉斯之暮年”）。此外，Diels 的文本暗示这句话的用意是表明阿尔克迈翁依赖毕达哥拉斯——这恰恰说明它不可能出自亚里士多德，因为亚里士多德刚把阿尔克迈翁与毕达哥拉斯学派区分开来，并对谁影响了谁表示怀疑（Primavesi 2012, 447–8）。即便这句话不太可能上溯到亚里士多德，他对谁影响谁的怀疑也表明阿尔克迈翁属于公元前六世纪末或五世纪初（Schofield 2012, 156），这与 Mansfeld（2013, 78, n. 1）采用的前 440 年的晚近定年相抵触。于是，一派学者把阿尔克迈翁著作的成书定在公元前 500 年左右（Burkert 1972, 292；Kirk, Raven, Schofield 1983, 339 [五世纪初]；Zhmud 2012a, 122 [不晚于前 490]），他因此约生于前 540 年。另一派认为他约生于前 510 年，其书便在前 470 年或更晚刊行（Guthrie 1962, 358 [前 480–440]；Lloyd 1991, 168 [前 490–430]）。无论哪种情形，阿尔克迈翁的写作可能都早于恩培多克勒、阿那克萨戈拉和菲洛劳斯，他与巴门尼德要么同时，要么更早。仅凭内证（即把他与其他思想家的学说相比较）来定年的种种尝试，得出的年代相差最远。Edelstein 说他可能生活于公元前五世纪末（1942, 372），Lebedev 则把他定在公元前六世纪末（1993）。Année 提出了最早的定年，认为阿尔克迈翁活动于公元前六世纪中叶，与毕达哥拉斯同时（2019: 101）。

en: 1.4 Alcmaeon’s Book and the Evidence for Its Contents
zh: 1.4 阿尔克迈翁的著作及其内容的文献依据

en: The ancient tradition assigns one book to Alcmaeon, which came to bear the traditional title of Presocratic treatises, *On Nature* (DK, A2), although this title probably does not go back to Alcmaeon himself. Favorinus’ report that Alcmaeon was the first to write such a treatise (DK, A1) is almost certainly wrong, since Anaximander wrote before Alcmaeon. Theophrastus’ detailed report of Alcmaeon’s account of the senses (DK, A5) and the fact that Aristotle wrote a treatise in response to Alcmaeon (D.L. V. 25) suggest that the book was available in the fourth century BCE. It is unclear whether Alcmaeon wrote in the Doric dialect of Croton or in the Ionic Greek of the first Presocratics (Burkert, 1972, 222, n. 21). The report that an Alcimon of Croton was the first to write animal fables might be a reference to a poet of a similar name. Fragment 5 in DK (“It is easier to be on one’s guard against an enemy than a friend.”) sounds very much like the moral of such a fable (Gomperz 1953, 64–5)[^gomperz-1953]. Diels and Kranz (=DK) identify five other fragments of Alcmaeon (Frs. 1, 1a, 2, 3, 4) and arrange the testimonia under 18 headings. Fragments 1a, 3 and 4, however, are really testimonia which use language of a later date, although some of Alcmaeon’s terminology is embedded in them. The three lines of Fragment 1, which probably began the book, and the half line in Fragment 2 are the only continuous texts of Alcmaeon. Another brief fragment/testimonium should be added to the material in DK: “the earth is the mother of plants and the sun their father” (Nicolaus Damascenus, *De plantis* I 2.44; see Kirk 1956 and Lebedev 1993)[^kirk-1956][^lebedev-1993]. There is also the possibility that Fr. 125 of the Spartan poet Alcman (“Experience is the beginning of learning.”) should, in fact, be assigned to Alcmaeon (Lanza 1965; Barnes 1982, 610; Année 2019, see 2.1 below)[^année-2019][^barnes-1982][^lanza-1965].
zh: 古代传统把一部书归于阿尔克迈翁，这部书后来获得了前苏格拉底论著的传统标题《论自然》（DK, A2），尽管这个标题很可能并非出自阿尔克迈翁本人。Favorinus 报告说阿尔克迈翁是第一个写这类论著的人（DK, A1），这几乎肯定是错的，因为阿那克西曼德写得更早。特奥弗拉斯托斯对阿尔克迈翁感觉学说的详细报告（DK, A5），以及亚里士多德写过一部回应阿尔克迈翁的专著（D.L. V. 25）这一事实，表明这部书在公元前四世纪尚可读到。阿尔克迈翁用的是克罗顿的多利亚方言，还是第一代前苏格拉底哲人的爱奥尼亚希腊语，不得而知（Burkert, 1972, 222, n. 21）。有一条报告说克罗顿的某位 Alcimon 是第一个写动物寓言的人，这或许是指一位名字相近的诗人。DK 中的残篇 5（“防备敌人比防备朋友容易。”）听上去非常像此类寓言的寓意（Gomperz 1953, 64–5）。Diels 和 Kranz（=DK）另认出阿尔克迈翁的五条残篇（Frs. 1, 1a, 2, 3, 4），并把学说汇编条目归入 18 个标题之下。不过，残篇 1a、3 和 4 实为使用了较晚语言的学说汇编条目，尽管其中嵌有阿尔克迈翁的某些术语。残篇 1 的三行——大概是全书的开篇——与残篇 2 的半行，是阿尔克迈翁仅有的连续文本。还有一条简短的残篇/学说汇编条目应当补入 DK 的材料：“大地是植物的母亲，太阳是它们的父亲”（Nicolaus Damascenus, De plantis I 2.44；见 Kirk 1956 与 Lebedev 1993）。此外，斯巴达诗人 Alcman 的残篇 125（“经验是学习的开端。”）也有可能实际上应归于阿尔克迈翁（Lanza 1965；Barnes 1982, 610；Année 2019，见下文 2.1）。

en: 2. Epistemology and Psychology
zh: 2 认识论与心理学

en: 2.1 The Limits of Knowledge
zh: 2.1 知识的界限

en: Alcmaeon began his book by defining the limits of human knowledge:
zh: 阿尔克迈翁在书的开头为人类知识划界：

en: Concerning things that are not perceptible [concerning mortal things] the gods have clarity, but insofar as it is possible for human beings to judge (*tekmairesthai*) … (DK, B1)
zh: 对于不可知觉的东西[对于会死的东西]，诸神有明晰的认识；就人所能凭征象推断（tekmairesthai）而言……（DK, B1）

en: Such apparent skepticism about human knowledge is characteristic of one strand of early Greek thought. Both Alcmaeon’s predecessors (e.g., Xenophanes B34) and his successors (e.g., Philolaus B6) made similar contrasts between divine and human knowledge, but in Alcmaeon’s case, as in these other cases, we do not have enough evidence to be sure what he intended. Most of the subjects that Alcmaeon went on to discuss in his book could not be settled by a direct appeal to sense perception (e.g., the functioning of the senses, the balance of opposites in the healthy body, the immortality of the soul). In this sense he was dealing largely with what is “not perceptible” (*aphanes*). Alcmaeon is decidedly not an extreme skeptic, however, in that he is willing to assign clear understanding about such things to the gods and by implication admits that even humans have clear understanding of what is directly perceptible. Moreover, while humans cannot attain clarity about what cannot be perceived, Alcmaeon thinks that they can make reasonable judgments from the signs that are presented to them by sensation (*tekmairesthai*). He thus takes the stance of the scientist who draws inferences from what can be perceived, and he implicitly rejects the claims of those who base their account of the world on the certainty of a divine revelation. The epistemic optimism of Alcmaeon’s empirical approach was emphasized by Fausti (1973) and more recently by Année (2019: 47–49, see further below).
zh: 这种对人类知识的明显怀疑态度，是早期希腊思想一个支脉的特征。阿尔克迈翁的前人（如色诺芬尼 B34）和后人（如菲洛劳斯 B6）都在神的知识与人的知识之间作过类似的对照，但与这些情形一样，我们掌握的证据不足以断定阿尔克迈翁的本意。阿尔克迈翁随后在书中讨论的多数论题，都无法靠诉诸感官知觉来解决（例如感官的机能、健康身体中对立的平衡、灵魂不朽）。在这个意义上，他处理的主要是“不可知觉的东西”（aphanes）。然而，阿尔克迈翁绝不是极端怀疑论者：他愿意把对这类事物的明晰认识归于诸神，并因此默认人类对直接可知觉的东西也有明晰认识。而且，虽然人无法对不可知觉的东西获得明晰认识，阿尔克迈翁认为人可以凭感觉呈现给你的征象作出合理的推断（tekmairesthai）。因此他采取的是科学家的立场：从可知觉的东西出发作推理；同时也默默拒斥了那些把对世界的说明建立在神圣启示之确定性上的人的主张。阿尔克迈翁经验主义进路的这种认识论乐观态度，先由 Fausti（1973）强调，近来又由 Année（2019: 47–49，详见下文）强调。

en: There are difficulties with the text of Fr. 1, which make its interpretation problematic. Some scholars exclude the material in brackets above because it is hard to see how to connect it to what precedes (e.g., Wachtler 1896)[^wachtler-1896], while others keep the material and suppose that we are to understand an “and” coordinating the phrase in brackets with what precedes it (e.g., DK 1952). Other scholars would place a semicolon or colon after “things that are not perceptible” so that up to the colon Alcmaeon is identifying his topic or the area of disagreement with this addressees, while after the colon he begins his own account (Kouloumentas 2018 following Gomperz; Wöhrle 2022)[^wöhrle-2022]. Here is Wöhrle’s suggestion translated into English:
zh: 残篇 1 的文本有种种困难，使其解释成问题。一些学者把上文方括号里的材料删去，因为很难看出它如何与前文衔接（如 Wachtler 1896）；另一些学者保留该材料，认为应理解为有一个“和”字把方括号内的短语与前文并列起来（如 DK 1952）。还有学者主张在“不可知觉的东西”之后放分号或冒号：冒号之前，阿尔克迈翁在点明他的主题或他与受献者的分歧所在；冒号之后，他才开始自己的论述（Kouloumentas 2018 承 Gomperz；Wöhrle 2022）。下面是 Wöhrle 的建议的英译：

en: Alcmaeon of Croton, son of Peirithous, said the following to Brotinus, Leon, and Bathyllus concerning things that are not perceptible: regarding mortal things the gods have certainty, as humans [we can] only draw conclusions.
zh: 克罗顿的阿尔克迈翁，佩里托奥斯之子，就不可知觉的东西对布罗提努斯、里昂和巴提卢斯说了如下的话：关于会死的东西，诸神有确切的把握，而我们人[只能]凭征象推断。

en: Gemelli Marciano (2007, 18–22), on the other hand, has suggested that the material in brackets above should be kept but made dependent on the immediately preceding phrase rather than coordinated with it, so that the fragment would read:
zh: 另一方面，Gemelli Marciano（2007, 18–22）建议：方括号里的材料应当保留，但从属于紧邻的前一个短语而非与之并列，于是残篇读作：

en: Concerning things that are not perceptible concerning mortals the gods have clarity, but insofar as it is possible for human beings to judge … (DK, B1)
zh: 对于不可知觉的东西中关于会死者的部分，诸神有明晰的认识；就人所能凭征象推断者而言……（DK, B1）

en: If we regard Alcmaeon as primarily a doctor or medical thinker, rather than as a cosmologist, “things that are not perceptible concerning mortals” is likely to refer to the interior of the body and hidden diseases. Passages in the Greek medical writings of the fifth century provide clear parallels for the difficulty of knowing about the interior of the body and invisible maladies (Gemelli Marciano 2007, 20–21)[^gemelli-2007]. On this reading Fr.1 is addressed to medical students. Parallels with medical treatises suggest that, after first raising difficulties about medical knowledge in these matters, Alcmaeon may have gone on to assert that these difficulties can be overcome with the proper teaching, the teaching that followed in his book. If this is the correct context in which to read the fragment, it is not so much about the limits of understanding as the success of medical teaching in overcoming apparent limits.
zh: 如果我们把阿尔克迈翁首先看作医生或医学思想家而非宇宙论者，那么“关于会死者的不可知觉的东西”很可能指身体的内部与隐藏的疾病。公元前五世纪希腊医学著作中的若干段落，为“难以认识身体内部与看不见的疾病”提供了清晰的平行文本（Gemelli Marciano 2007, 20–21）。按照这一读法，残篇 1 是对医学生们说的。与医学论著的平行文本提示：阿尔克迈翁在先就这些医学知识的困难发问之后，可能接着主张——凭借恰当的教授，这些困难可以被克服，而教授正是他书中随后要给出的内容。如果这才是读这条残篇的正确语境，那么它的要点与其说是理解的界限，不如说是医学教授能够克服表面上的界限。

en: Another approach which also keeps the material in brackets is that of Année (2019). On her intepretation Alcmaeon wrote a medical work largely in verse and the material in brackets is crucial, in part, to preserve the metrical structure. Année also thinks that Alcmaeon completed a four line incipit by perhaps “quoting” a line from the Spartan poet Alcman which fits into the meter of the passage of Alcmaeon (*Scholia vetera in Pindari Isthmionicas*, I, 56 = Alcman, fr. 63 Bergk; 125 Page; 293 Calame). On her view Alcmaeon’s Croton was heavily influenced by Spartan culture. She translates the resulting fragment as follows:
zh: 另一条同样保留方括号材料的路线来自 Année（2019）。在她的解读中，阿尔克迈翁写的主要是一部韵文医学著作，方括号里的材料对保存韵律结构至关重要。Année 还认为，阿尔克迈翁或许通过“引用”斯巴达诗人 Alcman 的一行诗补全了一个四行开头，该行恰好嵌入阿尔克迈翁这段文字的韵律（Scholia vetera in Pindari Isthmionicas, I, 56 = Alcman, fr. 63 Bergk; 125 Page; 293 Calame）。在她看来，阿尔克迈翁的克罗顿深受斯巴达文化影响。她把由此拼合的残篇译作：

en: About invisible things, about which—being mortal—the gods maintain certainty, it is up to us men to conjecture! Experience is indeed the beginning of knowledge.
zh: 论不可见的东西——它们身为会死者却为诸神所确知——且看我们凡人去猜想！经验诚然是知识的开端。

en: Her translation emphasizes the affirmative and parenetic character of the beginning of Alcmaeon’s work in contrast to the traditional reading which understands Alcmaeon to be stressing the limits of human knowledge.
zh: 她的翻译突出了阿尔克迈翁著作开篇的肯定性与劝勉性，与传统读法（把阿尔克迈翁理解为强调人类知识的界限）形成对照。

en: 2.2 Understanding and Empiricism
zh: 2.2 理解与经验主义

en: According to Theophrastus, Alcmaeon was the first Greek thinker to distinguish between sense perception and understanding and to use this distinction to separate animals, which only have sense perception, from humans, who have both sense perception and understanding (DK, B1a, A5). Alcmaeon is also the first to argue that the brain is the central organ of sensation and thought (DK, A5, A8, A10). There is no explicit evidence, however, as to what Alcmaeon meant by understanding. The word translated as understanding here is *suniêmi*, which in its earliest uses means “to bring together,” so that it is possible that Alcmaeon simply meant that humans are able to bring the information provided by the senses together in a way that animals cannot (Solmsen 1961, 151)[^solmsen-1961]. Animals have brains too, however, and thus might appear to be able to carry out the simple correlation of the evidence from the various senses, whereas the human ability to make inferences and judgments (DK, B1) appears to be a more plausible candidate for the distinctive activity of human intelligence. It is possible that we should use a passage in Plato’s *Phaedo* (96a–b = A11) to explicate further Alcmaeon’s epistemology. The passage is part of Socrates’ report of his early infatuation with natural science and with questions such as whether it is the blood, or air, or fire with which we think. He also reports the view that it is the brain that furnishes the sensations of hearing, sight, and smell. This corresponds very well with Alcmaeon’s view of the brain as the central sensory organ and, although Alcmaeon is not mentioned by name, many scholars think that Plato must be referring to him here. Socrates connects this view of the brain with an empiricist epistemology, which Aristotle will later adopt (*Posterior Analytics* 100a3 ff.). This epistemology involves three steps: first, the brain provides the sensations of hearing, sight and smell, then, memory and opinion arise from these, and finally, when memory and opinion achieve fixity, knowledge arises. Some scholars suppose that this entire epistemology is Alcmaeon’s (e.g., Barnes 1982, 149 ff.)[^barnes-1982], while others more cautiously note that we only have explicit evidence that Alcmaeon took the first step (e.g., Vlastos 1970, 47, n.8).
zh: 据特奥弗拉斯托斯，阿尔克迈翁是第一个区分感官知觉与理解的希腊思想家，并第一个用这一区分把只有感官知觉的动物与兼有二者的人分开（DK, B1a, A5）。阿尔克迈翁也是第一个论证大脑是感觉与思想的中枢器官的人（DK, A5, A8, A10）。然而，关于阿尔克迈翁所谓“理解”究竟指什么，并没有明确的证据。这里译作理解的词是 suniêmi，其最早的用法意为“汇合起来”，因此阿尔克迈翁有可能只是说：人能够以动物做不到的方式把感官提供的信息汇合起来（Solmsen 1961, 151）。可是动物也有大脑，因而看起来也能对来自各种感官的证据作简单关联；而人作出推断与判断的能力（DK, B1）倒是人类智能独特活动更为合理的候选者。我们或许可以借助柏拉图《斐多》中的一段话（96a–b = A11）进一步阐发阿尔克迈翁的认识论。这段话出自苏格拉底对自己早年迷恋自然科学的自述，那时他追问的问题包括：我们是用血液、气还是火来思考。苏格拉底还报告了另一种观点：是大脑提供了听觉、视觉和嗅觉。这与阿尔克迈翁“大脑是中枢感觉器官”的观点相当吻合；虽然柏拉图没有点名，许多学者认为他指的必是阿尔克迈翁。苏格拉底把这种大脑观与一种经验主义认识论联系在一起，亚里士多德后来采纳了它（《后分析篇》100a3 以下）。这一认识论分三步：首先，大脑提供听觉、视觉和嗅觉；然后，记忆和意见从这些感觉中产生；最后，当记忆和意见趋于固定，知识便产生了。一些学者认为这整套认识论都属于阿尔克迈翁（如 Barnes 1982, 149 以下），另一些学者则较谨慎地指出，我们只有明确证据证明阿尔克迈翁迈出了第一步（如 Vlastos 1970, 47, n.8）。

en: 2.3 Did Alcmaeon Practice Dissection?
zh: 2.3 阿尔克迈翁做过解剖吗？

en: Alcmaeon’s empiricism has sometimes been thought to have arisen from his experience as a practicing physician (Guthrie 1962)[^guthrie-1962]. He has also been hailed as the first to use dissection, but this is based on a hasty reading of the evidence. Calcidius, in his Latin commentary on Plato’s *Timaeus*, praises Alcmaeon, along with Callisthenes and Herophilus, for having brought many things to light about the nature of the eye (DK, A10). Most of what Calcidius goes on to describe, however, are the discoveries of Herophilus some two centuries after Alcmaeon (Lloyd 1975, Mansfeld 1975, Solmsen 1961)[^lloyd-1975][^mansfeld-1975][^solmsen-1961]. The only conclusions we can reasonably draw about Alcmaeon from the passage are that he excised the eyeball of an animal and observed *poroi* (channels, i.e. the optic nerve) leading from the eye in the direction of the brain (Lloyd 1975)[^lloyd-1975]. Theophrastus’ account of Alcmaeon’s theory of sensation implies that he thought that there were such channels leading from each of the senses to the brain:
zh: 有人有时认为，阿尔克迈翁的经验主义来自他行医的实践（Guthrie 1962）。他还被尊为解剖的第一人，但这是对证据的仓促解读。Calcidius 在他给柏拉图《蒂迈欧》所作的拉丁文注疏中，称赞阿尔克迈翁与卡利斯提尼（Callisthenes）、希罗菲卢斯（Herophilus）一道，揭示了关于眼睛本性的许多东西（DK, A10）。然而 Calcidius 接着描述的内容，大多是晚于阿尔克迈翁约两个世纪的希罗菲卢斯的发现（Lloyd 1975；Mansfeld 1975；Solmsen 1961）。从这段文字我们关于阿尔克迈翁能合理得出的唯一结论是：他切除过动物的眼球，并观察到从眼睛通向大脑方向的通道（poroi，即视神经）（Lloyd 1975）。特奥弗拉斯托斯对阿尔克迈翁感觉学说的报告则提示：他认为每种感官都有通向大脑的通道：

en: All the senses are connected in some way with the brain. As a result, they are incapacitated when it is disturbed or changes its place, for it then stops the channels, through which the senses operate. (DK, A5)
zh: 一切感官都以某种方式与大脑相连。因此，当大脑受到扰动或移位时，感官便陷于失能，因为大脑随即阻断了感官借以运作的通道。（DK, A5）

en: There is no evidence, however, that Alcmaeon dissected the eye itself or that he dissected the skull in order to trace the optic nerve all the way to the brain. Alcmaeon’s account of the other senses, far from suggesting that he carried out dissections in order to explain their function, implies that he did not (Lloyd 1975; for a partial critique of Lloyd see Perilli 2001)[^lloyd-1975][^perilli-2001]. Alcmaeon’s conclusion that all of the senses are connected to the brain may have been drawn from nothing more than the excision of the eye and the general observation that the sense organs for sight, hearing, smell, and taste are located on the head and appear connected to passages which lead inward towards the brain (Gomperz 1953, 69)[^gomperz-1953]. It is striking in this regard that Alcmaeon gave no account of touch (DK, A5), which is the only sense not specifically tied to the head. It would be a serious mistake then to say that Alcmaeon discovered dissection or that he was the father of anatomy, since there is no evidence that he used dissection systematically or even that he did more than excise a single eyeball.
zh: 然而，没有任何证据表明阿尔克迈翁解剖过眼睛本身，也没有证据表明他解剖颅骨以把视神经一路追到大脑。阿尔克迈翁对其余感官的说明，非但没有暗示他为了解释感官机能而作过解剖，反而暗示他没有这样做（Lloyd 1975；对 Lloyd 的部分批评见 Perilli 2001）。阿尔克迈翁“一切感官都连着大脑”的结论，可能不过是基于眼球的那次切除，加上这样的泛泛观察：视、听、嗅、味的感觉器官都位于头部，而且看起来与通向大脑内部的管道相连（Gomperz 1953, 69）。值得注意的是，阿尔克迈翁对触觉未作任何说明（DK, A5），而触觉恰恰是唯一不特定依附于头部的感觉。因此，断言阿尔克迈翁发现了解剖、或他是解剖学之父，将是严重的错误：没有证据表明他系统地使用过解剖，甚至没有证据表明他做的比切除一个眼球更多。

en: 2.4 Sense Perception
zh: 2.4 感官知觉

en: Theophrastus says that Alcmaeon did not explain sensation by the principle of like to like (i.e. by the likeness between the sense organ and what is perceived), a principle which was used by many early Greek thinkers (e.g., Empedocles). Unfortunately he gives no general account of how Alcmaeon did think sensation worked (DK, A5). Alcmaeon explained each of the individual senses with the exception of touch, but these accounts are fairly rudimentary. He regarded the eye as composed of water and fire and vision as taking place when what is seen is reflected in the gleaming and translucent part of the eye. Hearing arises when an external sound is first transmitted to the outer ear and then picked up by the empty space (*kenon*) in the inner ear, which transmits it to the brain. Taste occurs through the tongue, which being warm and soft dissolves things with its heat and, because of its loose texture, receives and transmits the sensation. Smell is the simplest of all. It occurs “at the same time as we breathe in, thus bringing the breath to the brain” (DK, A5).
zh: 特奥弗拉斯托斯说，阿尔克迈翁没有用“相似者感知相似者”的原则（即感觉器官与被感知物之间的相似）来解释感觉，而许多早期希腊思想家（如恩培多克勒）都使用这一原则。遗憾的是，他并没有给出阿尔克迈翁究竟如何理解感觉运作的一般说明（DK, A5）。阿尔克迈翁解释了除触觉之外的每一种感官，但这些说明都相当简陋。他认为眼睛由水和火构成，视觉的发生是因所见之物映现在眼睛明亮而半透明的部分上。听觉的发生，是外部声音先传到外耳，然后被内耳中的空腔（kenon）接收，再由它传给大脑。味觉经由舌头发生：舌头温暖而柔软，以热溶解食物，又因质地疏松而接收并传递感觉。嗅觉最简单，它“与我们吸气同时发生，由此把气息带给大脑”（DK, A5）。

en: 2.5 The Immortality of the Soul
zh: 2.5 灵魂不朽

en: Alcmaeon developed the first argument on record for the immortality of the soul, but the testimonia concerning it differ slightly from one another, and it appears to have been taken over and developed by Plato, so that it is very hard to determine exactly how to reconstruct Alcmaeon’s own argument. Barnes (1982, 116–120) and Hankinson (1998, 30–3) provide the most insightful analysis. Alcmaeon appears to have started from the assumption that the soul is always in motion. At one extreme we might suppose that Alcmaeon only developed the simple argument from analogy, which Aristotle assigns to him (*De An.* 405a29). The soul is like the heavenly bodies, which Alcmaeon regarded as divine and immortal (DK, A1, A12), in being always in motion, so it is also like them in being immortal. This is clearly fallacious, since it assumes that things that are alike in one respect will be alike in all others. The version in the doxographical tradition is more sophisticated (DK, A12). Alcmaeon thought that the soul moved itself in continual motion and was therefore immortal and like to the divine. The similarity to the divine is not part of the inference here but simply an illustrative comparison. However, Mansfeld has recently pointed out that the doxographical report in Aetius is just a paraphrase of Aristotle’s earlier report with the significant addition that the soul is self-moving. Examination of the context in Aetius shows that the self-motion of the soul, which is attested independently for Plato and Xenocrates, was projected back on Pythagoras and Thales, who are very unlikely to have held such a view. This context and Aristotle’s failure to assign self-motion to Alcmaeon makes it likely that the same projection occurred in the case of Alcmaeon, who thus is likely to have assigned continual motion but not self motion to the soul (Mansfeld 2014b, see also Laks 2018)[^laks-2018][^mansfeld-2014b]. The core of the simpler argument is the necessary truth that what is always in motion must be immortal. This is the assumption from which Plato starts his argument for the immortality of the soul at *Phaedrus* 245c, but how much of Plato’s analysis of what is always in motion can be assigned to Alcmaeon? Plato makes no mention of Alcmaeon in the passage. There are still serious questions for Alcmaeon, even on the more sophisticated version of the argument. We might well recognize that things with souls, i.e. things that are alive, are able to move themselves, and conclude that it is souls that bring this motion about. We might also conclude that the soul, as what moves something else, must be in motion itself (the synonymy principle of causation — See Aristotle *De Anima* 1 for a critique of this reasoning and principle). But why did Alcmaeon suppose that the soul must be always in motion? (Hankinson [1998, 32] provides two possible answers and discusses the difficulties with them.) Horn argues that there is no obvious meaning to the idea that the human soul is in continual motion so that Alcmaeon must be talking about a world soul, which has the continual motion of the heavens (2005, 157–8). However, Mansfeld rightly argues that Aristotle’s report on Alcmaeon’s view of the soul is clearly about the human soul; since the soul being discussed is said to be similar to the heavenly motions it has to be distinct from them (2014a). Finally, what sort of motion is being ascribed to souls? The natural assumption might be that the soul’s motion is thinking, but, at this early point in Greek thought, Alcmaeon was more likely to have thought that, if the soul is going to cause motion in space, it too must be in locomotion. Plato describes the soul as composed of two circles with contrary motions, which imitate the contrary motions of the fixed stars and the planets, so that the soul becomes a sort of orrery in the head (*Timaeus* 44d). It has been suggested that this image is borrowed from Alcmaeon (Barnes 1982, 118; Skemp 1942, 36 ff.)[^barnes-1982][^skemp-1942].
zh: 阿尔克迈翁提出了有案可查的第一个灵魂不朽论证，但关于它的学说汇编条目彼此略有出入，而且该论证似乎被柏拉图接过来加以发展，因此很难确定究竟该如何重构阿尔克迈翁本人的论证。Barnes（1982, 116–120）与 Hankinson（1998, 30–3）给出了最有洞见的分析。阿尔克迈翁似乎是从“灵魂永远在运动”这一假定出发的。在一个极端上，我们可以设想阿尔克迈翁只提出了亚里士多德归于他的那个简单的类比论证（《论灵魂》405a29）：灵魂像天体——阿尔克迈翁视天体为神圣而不朽（DK, A1, A12）——因为灵魂永远在运动，所以灵魂也像天体一样不朽。这显然是谬误的，因为它假定在一处相似的事物将在一切方面相似。学说汇编传统中的版本更为精致（DK, A12）：阿尔克迈翁认为灵魂以持续的运动推动它自身，因此不朽且类似于神圣者。在这里，“类似神圣者”不是推理的一部分，而只是打比方。然而，Mansfeld 近来指出，Aetius 的学说汇编报告只是对亚里士多德较早报告的转述，其重要增补是“灵魂自我运动”。考察 Aetius 的上下文可以看到：灵魂的自我运动，虽有独立证据归于柏拉图和色诺克拉底，却被倒推到毕达哥拉斯和泰勒斯头上，而这两位极不可能持这种观点。这一上下文，加上亚里士多德没有把自我运动归于阿尔克迈翁，使同样的倒推很可能也发生在阿尔克迈翁身上；因此阿尔克迈翁很可能只把持续的运动、而非自我运动归于灵魂（Mansfeld 2014b；另见 Laks 2018）。较简版本的论证核心是一条必然真理：永远在运动的东西必然不朽。柏拉图在《斐德罗》245c 为灵魂不朽论证正是从这个假定出发的；但柏拉图对“永远在运动者”的分析中，有多少可以归于阿尔克迈翁？柏拉图在该段没有提阿尔克迈翁的名字。即便在较精致的版本上，阿尔克迈翁仍面临严肃的问题。我们大概会承认：有灵魂的东西（即活物）能够自己运动，并由此断定是灵魂造成了这种运动；我们也可能断定，灵魂作为推动他物者，自身必定在运动（因果同义原则——对该推理与原则的批评见《论灵魂》第一卷）。可是阿尔克迈翁凭什么认为灵魂必须永远在运动？（Hankinson [1998, 32] 给出了两种可能的回答，并讨论了它们的困难。）Horn 主张，“人的灵魂处于持续运动中”这个想法没有明显的意义，因此阿尔克迈翁说的必是世界灵魂，它拥有天球的持续运动（2005, 157–8）。然而 Mansfeld 正确地指出：亚里士多德关于阿尔克迈翁灵魂观的报告，讲的显然是人的灵魂；既然被讨论的灵魂被说成类似于天球的运行，它就必须与天球有别（2014a）。最后，被归于灵魂的究竟是哪种运动？自然的设想或许是思维，但在希腊思想的这个早期阶段，阿尔克迈翁更可能认为：如果灵魂要引起空间中的运动，它自身也必须作位移运动。柏拉图把灵魂描述为由两个作相反运动的圆圈组成，模仿恒星与行星的相反运动，于是灵魂成了脑袋里的一台太阳系仪（《蒂迈欧》44d）。有人提示这一意象得自阿尔克迈翁（Barnes 1982, 118；Skemp 1942, 36 以下）。

en: In Fragment 2, Alcmaeon is reported to have said that:
zh: 在残篇 2 中，据报告阿尔克迈翁说过：

en: Human beings perish because they are not able to join their beginning to their end.
zh: 人之所以会死，是因为他们不能把开端与结尾连接起来。

en: At first sight, this assertion might appear to conflict with Alcmaeon’s belief that the soul is immortal. It seems likely, however, that Alcmaeon distinguished between human beings as individual body-soul composites, which do perish, and as souls, which do not (Barnes 1982, 115)[^barnes-1982]. There is no evidence about what Alcmaeon thought happened to the soul, when the body perished, however. Did he believe in reincarnation as the Pythagoreans did? No ancient source associates Alcmaeon with reincarnation. His sharp distinction between animals and human beings may suggest that he did not believe in it (Guthrie 1962: 354)[^guthrie-1962], but he could have restricted it to humans. He might have thought that the soul joined other divine beings in the heavens. The point of Fragment 2 may be that, whereas the heavenly bodies do join their beginnings to their ends in circular motion, humans are not able to join their end in old age to their beginning in childhood, i.e. human life does not have a cyclical structure. We might even suppose that the soul tries to impose such a structure on the body from its own circular motion but ultimately fails (Guthrie 1962, 353)[^guthrie-1962]. It has been rather speculatively suggested that, since Alcmaeon explains sleep and waking by the blood retreating into the inner vessels and then expanding again into the outer vessels (see 3.2 below), it may be that this “circular motion” of the blood that fails in death (Kouloumentas 2018b)[^kouloumentas-2018b].
zh: 初看之下，这句话似乎与阿尔克迈翁灵魂不朽的信念相冲突。然而很可能，阿尔克迈翁区分了作为个别身心复合体的人（它们会死）与作为灵魂的人（灵魂不死）（Barnes 1982, 115）。不过，关于身体灭亡时灵魂的遭遇，阿尔克迈翁如何设想，没有任何证据。他像毕达哥拉斯学派那样相信轮回吗？没有古代文献把阿尔克迈翁与轮回联系起来。他把动物与人截然二分，可能暗示他不信轮回（Guthrie 1962: 354），但他也可能把轮回限于人类。他也许认为灵魂去天上与其他神圣存在者会合。残篇 2 的要点或许在于：天体在圆周运动中确实把开端与结尾连接起来，而人不能把老年的结尾与童年的开端连接起来，也就是说，人的生命没有循环结构。我们甚至可以设想：灵魂试图把自己圆周式的运行结构加诸身体，但最终失败（Guthrie 1962, 353）。还有人相当思辨地提出：既然阿尔克迈翁用血液退入体内较粗血管、再重新扩散到体表来解释睡眠与醒来（见下文 3.2），那么死亡时失效的，可能正是血液的这种“圆周运动”（Kouloumentas 2018b）。

en: 3. Medical Doctrines
zh: 3 医学学说

en: 3.1 Health and Disease
zh: 3.1 健康与疾病

en: Fragment 4 (DK 12B4) presents Alcmaeon’s account of health and disease:
zh: 残篇 4（DK 12B4）给出了阿尔克迈翁对健康与疾病的说明：

en: Alcmaeon said that the equality (*isonomia*) of the powers (wet, dry, cold, hot, bitter, sweet, etc.) maintains health but that monarchy among them produces disease.
zh: 阿尔克迈翁说，诸力量（湿、干、冷、热、苦、甜等等）的平等（isonomia）维系健康，而它们中间的专权（monarchia）则产生疾病。

en: This is, in fact, not a fragment but a testimonium and much of the language comes from the doxographical tradition rather than Alcmaeon. The report goes on to say that Alcmaeon thought that disease arose because of an excess of heat or cold, which in turn arose because of an excess or deficiency in nutrition. Disease is said to arise in the blood, the marrow, or the brain. It can also be caused by external factors such as the water, the locality, toil, or violence. The idea that health depends on a balance of opposed factors in the body is a commonplace in Greek medical writers. Although Alcmaeon is the earliest figure to whom such a conception of health is attributed, it may well be that he is not presenting an original thesis but rather drawing on the earlier medical tradition in Croton. Perhaps what is distinctive to Alcmaeon is the use of the specific political metaphor and most scholars (e.g., Sassi 2007, 198; Jouanna 1999, 327; Kouloumentas 2014, 871)[^jouanna-1999][^kouloumentas-2014][^sassi-2007] agree that the political terminology (*isonomia*, *monarchia*) goes back to him. Indeed, these terms are not found elsewhere in the Greek medical tradition. Just as Anaximander explained the order of the cosmos in terms of justice in the city-state, so Alcmaeon used a political metaphor to explain the order of the human body. Plato will later (*Timaeus* 82a) also explain bodily health as an equilibrium of the elements and use a political metaphor to account for disease as resulting from the “greed” or “overreaching” (*pleonexia*) of the elements. It is commonly recognized that *isonomia* (equality) is not a specific form of government but rather a concept of political equality in terms of which forms of government are evaluated (Ostwald 1969, 108; Meier 1990, 162 calls it a “yardstick”, Vlastos 1981, 173–74 a “banner”)[^meier-1990][^ostwald-1969]. Its primary application is to democracies (Herodotus III.80) but it is also applied to moderate oligarchies that have democratic features (Thucydides III. 62.3–4). Although a significant number of scholars argue that there is a purely aristocratic application for *isonomia* as the equality of aristocratic peers in opposition to a tyrant (e.g., Raaflaub 2004: 95; Zhmud 2012a: 358)[^raaflaub-2004][^zhmud-2012a], one of the most noted early adherents of this view later abandoned it (Ehrenberg 1956: 67)[^ehrenberg-1956] and it appears more likely that the term * isonomia* originated with the radical democracy which emerged in Athens in the late sixth century and was only applied in a secondary sense to moderate oligarchies (Vlastos 1973, 175–7; Ostwald 1969, 99–106)[^ostwald-1969]. Is Alcmaeon’s use of the term simply descriptive of the equality of powers that is necessary for the healthy body, or does his use of the term to describe health suggest that he was in sympathy with radical democracy (Vlastos 1953, 363)[^vlastos-1953]? We simply have no direct evidence for Alcmaeon’s political views. However, Aristotle emphasizes that Alcmaeon posited an indefinite number of opposites as active in the human body in contrast to the Pythagoreans who specified ten pairs (see 4.2 below), which suggests that Alcmaeon’s “body” politic was not an oligarchy with a numerically defined group of peers but rather a democracy which gave equality to the full range of opposites. Mansfeld has recently argued that scholars are wrong to ascribe the key terms * isonomia* and *monarchia* to Alcmaeon (Mansfeld 2014a)[^mansfeld-2014a]. Such a metaphorical use of *isonomia* is unparalleled at this early date and is much more likely to have been introduced later in the doxographical tradition. Moreover, *monarchia* may have been introduced by a doxographer familiar with its use in the famous debate on constitutions in Herodotus (III 80–3), where *isonomia* also appears (III 80). Mansfeld concludes that this origin of the terms from the doxography is more likely than assuming influence on Alcmaeon from the reforms of Cleisthenes. The difficulty with Mansfeld’s approach is that the striking thing about the report on Alcmaeon is precisely the political metaphor and it seems more plausible that his views were introduced into the doxography because of that metaphor than that his views were typical Greek views on disease and the metaphor only arose as an artefact of the doxographical tradition. If he did introduce the political metaphor then it is as probable as not that he used the terms ascribed to him, especially since both appear only a little later in Herodotus, although not with a metaphorical sense.
zh: 这其实不是一条残篇而是一条学说汇编条目，其语言多出自学说史传统而非阿尔克迈翁本人。报告接着说，阿尔克迈翁认为疾病起于热或冷的过量，而热或冷的过量又起于营养的过剩或不足。疾病据说发生于血液、骨髓或大脑，也可能由水、居住地、劳苦或暴力等外部因素引起。“健康取决于体内对立因素的平衡”这一观念，在希腊医学作家中是老生常谈。虽然阿尔克迈翁是被归于这种健康观最早的人物，但他很可能并非提出原创论题，而是取用于克罗顿更早的医学传统。或许真正属于阿尔克迈翁的独特之处，是那个具体的政治隐喻；多数学者（如 Sassi 2007, 198；Jouanna 1999, 327；Kouloumentas 2014, 871）同意，政治术语（isonomia、monarchia）可以上溯到他。确实，这些术语在希腊医学传统中别无他见。正如阿那克西曼德用城邦中的“正义”解释宇宙的秩序，阿尔克迈翁也用政治隐喻来解释人体的秩序。柏拉图后来（《蒂迈欧》82a）同样把身体健康解释为诸元素的均衡，并用政治隐喻把疾病归因于诸元素的“贪婪”或“逾越”（pleonexia）。人们通常承认，isonomia（平等）不是一种具体的政体形式，而是一个政治平等的概念，各政体形式都依它来评价（Ostwald 1969, 108；Meier 1990, 162 称之为“标尺”，Vlastos 1981, 173–74 称之为“旗帜”）。它首要地适用于民主制（希罗多德 III.80），但也适用于带有民主特征的温和寡头制（修昔底德 III. 62.3–4）。虽然有相当一批学者主张 isonomia 还有纯粹的贵族式用法——即贵族同侪之间相对于僭主的平等（如 Raaflaub 2004: 95；Zhmud 2012a: 358），但这一观点最早的支持者之一后来放弃了自己的看法（Ehrenberg 1956: 67）；更可能的是，isonomia 一词起源于公元前六世纪末雅典兴起的激进民主，只是被次要地应用于温和寡头制（Vlastos 1973, 175–7；Ostwald 1969, 99–106）。阿尔克迈翁对该词的使用，仅仅是在描述健康身体所必需的诸力量的平等呢，还是他用这个词描述健康，暗示他同情激进民主（Vlastos 1953, 363）？我们根本没有关于阿尔克迈翁政治观点的直接证据。不过，亚里士多德强调：阿尔克迈翁设定人体内起作用的对立是无限数的，而毕达哥拉斯学派指定了十对（见下文 4.2）——这提示阿尔克迈翁的“身体”政体不是寡头制（其同侪在数目上有定限），而是把平等给予全部对立范围的民主制。Mansfeld 近来主张，学者们把 isonomia 与 monarchia 这两个关键词归于阿尔克迈翁是错误的（Mansfeld 2014a）。在这种早期年代，对 isonomia 的这种隐喻用法没有先例，更可能是后来才引入学说史传统的。而且 monarchia 可能是由某位熟悉它在希罗多德著名政体辩论（III 80–3）中用法的学说汇编家引入的——isonomia 在那里也出现了（III 80）。Mansfeld 的结论是：这两个术语出自学说汇编，比假定克利斯提尼改革影响了阿尔克迈翁更可信。Mansfeld 路线的困难在于：关于阿尔克迈翁的报告最惹眼的东西恰恰是那个政治隐喻；与其说他的观点是关于疾病的典型希腊观点、隐喻只是学说史传统的产物，不如说他的观点正因为这个隐喻才被写入学说汇编。如果政治隐喻确系他本人引入，那么他使用归于他的那些术语，就是五五开的事——尤其是因为这两个词仅在稍晚的希罗多德书中出现，尽管不是隐喻意义。

en: 3.2 Sleep, Embryology, and the Use of Analogy
zh: 3.2 睡眠、胚胎学与类比的使用

en: Alcmaeon is the first to raise a series of questions in human and animal physiology that later become stock problems, which every thinker tries to address. He thus sets the initial agenda for Greek physiology (Longrigg 1993, 54–7; Lloyd 1966, 322 ff.)[^lloyd-1966][^longrigg-1993]. He said that sleep is produced by the withdrawal of the blood away from the surface of the body to the larger (“blood-flowing”) vessels and that we awake when the blood diffuses throughout the body again (DK, A18). Death occurs when the blood withdraws entirely. Hippocratic writers (*Epid*. VI 5.15) and Aristotle (*H.A.* 521a15) both seem to have adopted Alcmaeon’s account of sleep. It is very unlikely, however, that Alcmaeon distinguished between veins (the “blood-flowing vessels”) and arteries, as some have claimed. It is more likely that he simply distinguished between larger more interior blood vessels as opposed to smaller ones close to the surface (Lloyd 1991, 177)[^lloyd-1991]. He probably argued that human seed was drawn from the brain (DK, A13). It has recently been suggested (König 2019)[^könig-2019], however, that he instead thought 1) that sperm came from the whole body, 2) that the brain was its transit port and 3) that it was ultimately a product of digestion. But no ancient source directly assigns any of these doctrines to Alcmaeon and the arguments in favor of them are very indirect. Contrary to a popular Greek view, which regarded the father alone as providing seed, a view that would be followed by Aristotle (Lloyd 1983, 86 ff.)[^lloyd-1983], Alcmaeon may have argued that both parents contribute seed (DK, A13) and that the child takes the sex of the parent who contributes the most seed (DK, A14). It has recently been suggested, however, that our sole source for these views (Censorinus) is mistaken and that, while Alcmaeon thought that both the male and female contributed to the child, only the male contributed seed (Leitao 2012: 278–79)[^leitao-2012], the female contributing menses. According to one report, Alcmaeon thought that the head was the first part of the embryo to develop, although another report has him confessing that he did not have definite knowledge in this area, because no one is able to perceive what is formed first in the infant (DK, A13). These reports are not inconsistent and conform to the epistemology with which Alcmaeon began his book. It is plausible to suppose that he regarded the development of the embryo as one of the imperceptibles about which we can have no certain knowledge. On the other hand, he may have regarded it as a reasonable inference that the part of the body which controls it in life, i.e., the brain, developed first in the womb. Dissection is of obvious relevance to the debate about the development of the embryo, and Alcmaeon’s failure to appeal to dissection of animals in this case is further evidence that he did not employ it as a regular method (Lloyd 1979, 163)[^lloyd-1979]. Alcmaeon studied not just humans but also animals and plants. He gave an explanation of the sterility of mules (DK, B3) and, if we can believe Aristotle, thought that goats breathed through their ears (DK, A7). More significantly, he used analogies with animals and plants in developing his accounts of human physiology. Thus, the pubic hair that develops when human males are about to produce seed for the first time at age fourteen is analogous to the flowering of plants before they produce seed (DK, A15); milk in mammals is analogous to egg white in birds (DK, A16). The infant in the womb absorbs nutrients through its entire body, like a sponge, although another report suggests that the embryo already feeds through its mouth (DK, A17). However, the text of the latter report should perhaps be amended from *stomati* [mouth] to *sômati* [body], thus removing the contradiction (Olivieri 1919, 34)[^olivieri-1919]. Analogies such as these will become a staple item in later Greek biological treatises, but Alcmaeon is one of the earliest figures in this tradition.
zh: 阿尔克迈翁第一个提出了一系列人与动物生理学的问题，它们后来成为每个思想家都要应对的常见问题；他为希腊生理学定了最初的议程（Longrigg 1993, 54–7；Lloyd 1966, 322 以下）。他说，睡眠由血液从身体表面撤回到较粗的（“行血的”）血管而产生，当血液重新扩散全身时我们便醒来（DK, A18）。血液全部退回时，死亡便来临。希波克拉底派作家（Epid. VI 5.15）和亚里士多德（H.A. 521a15）看来都采纳了阿尔克迈翁的睡眠说明。然而，阿尔克迈翁是否如有些人宣称的那样区分了静脉（“行血的血管”）与动脉，极可怀疑。更可能的是，他只是区分了较粗、较靠体内的血管与靠近体表的较细血管（Lloyd 1991, 177）。他可能主张人的种子取自大脑（DK, A13）。不过近来有人提出（König 2019），他反而认为：1）精子来自全身；2）大脑是它的转运港；3）它最终是消化的产物。但没有古代文献把这些学说直接归于阿尔克迈翁，支持它们的论证都非常间接。与一种流行的希腊观点——只有父亲提供种子，亚里士多德后来也持此见（Lloyd 1983, 86 以下）——相反，阿尔克迈翁可能主张父母双方都贡献种子（DK, A13），而孩子取贡献较多种子一方的性别（DK, A14）。然而近来也有人提出，我们关于这些观点的唯一来源（Censorinus）弄错了：阿尔克迈翁虽然认为男女都对孩子有贡献，但只有男性贡献种子（Leitao 2012: 278–79），女性贡献的是经血。据一条报告，阿尔克迈翁认为头是胚胎最先发育的部分；另一条报告则让他承认在这个领域没有确定的知识，因为没有人能知觉到婴儿身上先形成的是什么（DK, A13）。这两条报告并不矛盾，而且与阿尔克迈翁在书首的认识论相合：可以合理地设想，他把胚胎的发育算作我们无法确切认识的不可知觉者之一。另一方面，他也可能认为这是一个合理的推断：在生活中控制身体的那部分（即大脑）在子宫里先发育。解剖与胚胎发育之争有明显的关联，而阿尔克迈翁在此没有诉诸动物解剖，进一步证明他没有把解剖当作常规方法（Lloyd 1979, 163）。阿尔克迈翁不只研究人，也研究动物和植物。他解释过骡子不育的原因（DK, B3），而且如果我们能相信亚里士多德，他还认为山羊用耳朵呼吸（DK, A7）。更重要的是，他在阐发人的生理学时运用了与动物和植物的类比。于是，男性在十四岁左右将首次产种时长出的阴毛，被类比于植物结实之前的花开（DK, A15）；哺乳动物的乳汁被类比于鸟类的蛋清（DK, A16）。子宫中的胎儿像海绵一样通过全身吸收营养，尽管另一条报告说胚胎已经用嘴进食（DK, A17）。不过，后一条报告的文本或许应当从 stomati[嘴] 改为 sômati[身体]，矛盾便告消除（Olivieri 1919, 34）。此类类比日后将成为希腊生物学论著的家常便饭，而阿尔克迈翁正是这一传统最早的人物之一。

en: 4. Cosmology
zh: 4 宇宙论

en: 4.1 Astronomy
zh: 4.1 天文学

en: As indicated in section 1 above, there is considerable controversy as to whether and to what extent Alcmaeon was a Presocratic cosmologist. Certainly the evidence for his cosmology is meager. There are three references to his astronomical theory (DK, A4). He is reported to have recognized that the planets have a motion from west to east opposite to the motion of the fixed stars. Some doubt that such knowledge was available at the beginning of the fifth century (Dicks 1970, 75)[^dicks-1970]. Others suggest that Anaximenes, in the second half of the sixth century, had already distinguished between the fixed stars, which are nailed to the ice-like vault of the sky, and planets which float on the air like leaves (DK13A7; Burkert 1972, 311). Alcmaeon’s belief that the sun is flat is another possible connection to Anaximenes, who said that the sun was flat like a leaf (DK13A15). Finally, another similarity to Ionian astronomy is found in Alcmaeon’s agreement with Heraclitus that lunar eclipses were to be explained by the turning of a bowl-shaped moon. One might have expected, however, that the moon would be flat like the sun (West 1971, 175)[^west-1971].
zh: 如上文第 1 节所示，阿尔克迈翁是否是前苏格拉底宇宙论者、在多大程度上是，存在相当大的争议。可以肯定的是，关于他的宇宙论证据很贫乏。他的天文学理论有三处引证（DK, A4）。据报告，他认识到行星有一种与恒星相反的、自西向东的运动。有人怀疑这样的知识在公元前五世纪初是否可得（Dicks 1970, 75）。另一些人指出，阿那克西美尼早在公元前六世纪下半叶就已经区分了钉在冰封天穹上的恒星与像树叶一样漂浮在气中的行星（DK13A7；Burkert 1972, 311）。阿尔克迈翁认为太阳是扁平的，这也是与阿那克西美尼的一个可能联系，后者说太阳像叶子一样扁平（DK13A15）。最后，阿尔克迈翁同意赫拉克利特，用碗状月亮的翻转来解释月食，这又是一个与爱奥尼亚天文学的相似点。不过，人们本可期望月亮也像太阳一样是扁平的（West 1971, 175）。

en: 4.2 Opposites
zh: 4.2 对立

en: Did Alcmaeon present a cosmogony or cosmology in terms of the interaction of pairs of opposites? Such a cosmology could be seen as yet another connection to earlier speculation in Ionia, since Anaximander’s cosmos is based on the “justice” established between conflicting opposites (DK12B1). Heraclitus is also a possible influence on Alcmaeon, since he seems to envisage an endless process of opposites turning into one another such as is proposed for Alcmaeon (Mansfeld 2014a, 91–2)[^mansfeld-2014a]. Aristotle provides the primary evidence for such a cosmology in Alcmaeon (*Metaph*. 986a22 ff. = A3), but he compares Alcmaeon not to the Ionians but to a group of Pythagoreans who proposed a table of ten pairs of opposites. Alcmaeon agrees with these Pythagoreans in regarding the opposites as principles of things. Aristotle complains, however, that Alcmaeon did not arrive at a definite set of opposites but spoke haphazardly of white, black, sweet, bitter, good, bad, large, and small, and only threw in vague comments about the remaining opposites. It may well be that Alcmaeon’s primary discussion of opposites was in relation to his account of the human body (DK, B4; see the discussion of his medical theories above). Aristotle’s language supports this suggestion to some extent, when he summarizes Alcmaeon’s view as that “the majority of *human* things (*tôn anthrôpinôn*) are in pairs” (*Metaph*. 986a31). Isocrates (DK, A3) says that Alcmaeon, in contrast to Empedocles, who postulated four elements, said that there were only two, and, according to a heterodox view, Alcmaeon posited fire and earth as basic elements (Lebedev 1993)[^lebedev-1993]. Most scholars follow Aristotle, however, in supposing that Alcmaeon thought that the human body and perhaps the cosmos is constituted from the balance of an indefinite number of opposites. Some have seen Alcmaeon’s unwillingness to adopt a fixed set of opposites as a virtue and a further sign of his empiricism, which is willing to accept that the world is less tidy than theoretical constructs, such as the Pythagorean table of opposites, would suggest (Guthrie 1962, 346)[^guthrie-1962].
zh: 阿尔克迈翁是否用成对对立的相互作用提出过一种宇宙发生论或宇宙论？这样的宇宙论可以看作他与爱奥尼亚早期思辨的又一联系，因为阿那克西曼德的宇宙就建立在相互冲突的对立之间确立的“正义”之上（DK12B1）。赫拉克利特也可能是阿尔克迈翁的灵感来源，因为他似乎设想了对立无休止地相互转化的过程，而类似的构想也被归于阿尔克迈翁（Mansfeld 2014a, 91–2）。亚里士多德提供了阿尔克迈翁有这种宇宙论的首要证据（《形而上学》986a22 以下 = A3），但他拿来与阿尔克迈翁比较的不是爱奥尼亚人，而是一群提出了十对对立表的毕达哥拉斯学派成员。阿尔克迈翁与这些毕达哥拉斯学派成员一致，把对立当作万物的本原。然而亚里士多德抱怨说，阿尔克迈翁没有得出一个确定的对立集合，而是随手拈来地谈论白与黑、甜与苦、好与坏、大与小，对其余对立只丢下一些含糊的评论。很可能，阿尔克迈翁对对立的主要讨论是围绕他对人体的说明展开的（DK, B4；见上文 3.1）。亚里士多德的措辞在某种程度上支持这一猜测：他把阿尔克迈翁的观点概括为“人的事情（tôn anthrôpinôn）大多是成对的”（《形而上学》986a31）。Isocrates（DK, A3）说，与设定四元素的恩培多克勒不同，阿尔克迈翁说元素只有两个；据一个非正统观点，阿尔克迈翁设定火与土为基本元素（Lebedev 1993）。然而多数学者跟随亚里士多德，认为阿尔克迈翁设想人体、也许还有宇宙，由无限多对立的平衡构成。有人把阿尔克迈翁不肯采用固定对立集合看作一种美德，也是他经验主义的又一标志：他愿意承认，世界不像毕达哥拉斯对立表那样的理论构造所暗示的那么齐整（Guthrie 1962, 346）。

en: 5. Importance and Influence
zh: 5 地位与影响

en: Alcmaeon had been somewhat neglected in recent scholarship on early Greek philosophy (e.g., he hardly appears in Curd and Graham 2008, Long 1999 and Taylor 1997, the most recent surveys of the subject)[^curd-2008][^long-1999][^taylor-1997], but both Guthrie 1962, Zhmud 2012a and 2014 and now Année 2019 and Wöhrle 2022 show his importance. There would appear to be several reasons for his earlier neglect. First, what remains of Alcmaeon’s book has little to say on the metaphysical questions about the first principles of the cosmos and about being, which have dominated recent scholarship on the Presocratics. Second, doubts about his date and about the focus of his investigations have made it difficult to place him in the development of early Greek thought. Finally, a more accurate appreciation of his use of dissection has deflated some of the hyperbolic claims in earlier scholarship about his originality. The extent of his originality and the importance of his influence depend to a degree on his dating. An extremely late dating for his activity (after 450 BCE) makes him appear to espouse the typical views of the age rather than to break new ground. If he was active in the early fifth century, his views are much more original. That Aristotle wrote a separate treatise in response to Alcmaeon argues in favor of his originality. He should probably be regarded as a pioneer in applying a political metaphor to the balance of opposites that constitute the healthy human body. The range of his work in biology is remarkable for the early fifth century and he may have initiated a physiological emphasis in Greek philosophy which was not present in Ionian philosophers, such as Anaximander and Anaximenes, and set the agenda in this area for later Presocratics (Zhmud 2012a, 366)[^zhmud-2012a]. It is sometimes said that his conception of *poroi* (channels), which connect the sense organs to the brain, influenced Empedocles’ theory of *poroi*, but the theories may share no more than the name. In Empedocles, all materials have pores in them, which determine whether they mix well with other objects. Sense organs also have pores, but these function not to connect the sense organ to the seat of intelligence (which for Empedocles is the heart) but to determine whether the sense organ can receive the effluences that are poured forth by external objects (Solmsen 1961, 157; Wright 1981, 230)[^solmsen-1961][^wright-1981]. Alcmaeon’s influence was significant in three final ways: 1) His identification of the brain as the seat of human intelligence influenced Philolaus (DK, B13), the Hippocratic Treatise, *On the Sacred Disease*, and Plato (*Timaeus* 44d), although a number of thinkers including Empedocles and Aristotle continued to regard the heart as the seat of perception and intelligence. 2) His empiricist epistemology may lie behind important passages in Plato (*Phaedo* 96b) and Aristotle (*Posterior Analytics* 100a). 3) He developed the first argument on record for the immortality of the soul, which may have influenced Plato’s argument in the *Phaedrus* (245c ff.).
zh: 晚近关于早期希腊哲学的研究多少冷落了阿尔克迈翁（例如在最新的几部综述 Curd and Graham 2008、Long 1999 与 Taylor 1997 中，他几乎不露面），但 Guthrie 1962、Zhmud 2012a 与 2014，以及现在的 Année 2019 与 Wöhrle 2022，都显示了他的重要性。他先前受冷落，似乎有几个原因。第一，阿尔克迈翁的著作遗存对宇宙第一本原与存在这些形而上学问题着墨很少，而晚近的前苏格拉底研究恰以这些问题为主轴。第二，对他的年代和研究重心的怀疑，使人难以在早期希腊思想的发展中为他安放位置。最后，对他的解剖使用更准确的评价，挫掉了早先学术中关于其原创性的一些夸张说法。他的原创性程度与影响的重要性，在某种程度上取决于他的定年。把他的活动定得极晚（公元前 450 年以后），会使他显得只是在附和那个时代的典型观点而非开辟新地。如果他活动于公元前五世纪初，他的观点就原创得多。亚里士多德专门写了一部书回应阿尔克迈翁，这一事实本身就是其原创性的证据。他大概应被视为第一个把政治隐喻用于构成健康人体的对立平衡的人。他在生物学方面的工作范围，对公元前五世纪初而言令人瞩目；他或许在希腊哲学中开创了一种爱奥尼亚哲人（如阿那克西曼德和阿那克西美尼）那里所没有的生理学取向，并为后来的前苏格拉底哲人在这一领域定了议程（Zhmud 2012a, 366）。有时人们说，他那种把感觉器官与大脑连接起来的通道（poroi）概念影响了恩培多克勒的通道理论，但两种理论之间可能共享的只有名字。在恩培多克勒那里，一切材料都有孔隙，孔隙决定它们能否与其他对象良好混合；感觉器官也有孔隙，但其功能不是把感觉器官连到智慧的所在（对恩培多克勒来说是心脏），而是决定感觉器官能否接收外部对象倾泻而出的流射物（Solmsen 1961, 157；Wright 1981, 230）。阿尔克迈翁的影响最后还体现在三个方面：1）他把大脑确认为人类智慧之所在，影响了菲洛劳斯（DK, B13）、希波克拉底论文《论圣病》以及柏拉图（《蒂迈欧》44d），尽管包括恩培多克勒和亚里士多德在内的一批思想家仍把心脏当作知觉与智慧的所在。2）他的经验主义认识论可能藏在柏拉图（《斐多》96b）与亚里士多德（《后分析篇》100a）的重要段落背后。3）他提出了有案可查的第一个灵魂不朽论证，可能影响了柏拉图在《斐德罗》（245c 以下）中的论证。
